text: The proverbs of Solomon. A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish son is his mother's grief.
Treasures gained by wickedness are worthless, but righteousness rescues from death.
The LORD does not let the righteous go hungry, but he thwarts the craving of the wicked.
A slack hand brings poverty, but the hand of the diligent brings wealth.
Whoever gathers in summer is a wise son; whoever sleeps through the harvest is a son who brings shame.
Blessings rest on the head of the righteous, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
The memory of the righteous is a blessing, but the name of the wicked will rot.
The wise in heart accepts instruction, but the babbling fool comes to ruin.
Whoever walks in integrity walks in safety, but whoever takes crooked paths will be found out.

versions.text: Whoever walks in integrity walks secure, but whoever takes crooked paths will be found out.
versions.explanation: "Walks secure" uses the adjective adverbially, which sounds clipped when read aloud. Hebrew בֶּטַח is a noun ("security, safety"), so "walks in safety" is both more accurate and smoother for oral reading.

text: Whoever winks the eye causes pain, and the babbling fool comes to ruin.^f The second line repeats verse 8; some ancient witnesses read: but one who reproves openly makes peace.

versions.text: Whoever winks the eye causes pain, and the babbling fool comes to ruin.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew second line is identical to verse 8b, while ancient witnesses preserve a different second line. A short footnote explains the repetition for readers who notice it.

text: The mouth of the righteous is a fountain of life, but the mouth of the wicked conceals violence.
Hatred stirs up strife, but love covers all offenses.
On the lips of the discerning wisdom is found, but a rod is for the back of one who lacks sense.
The wise store up knowledge, but the mouth of a fool invites ruin.
The wealth of the rich is his fortified city; poverty is the ruin of the poor.
The wages of the righteous lead to life; the gain of the wicked leads to sin.
Whoever heeds discipline is on the path to life, but whoever ignores correction leads others astray.
Whoever conceals hatred has lying lips, and whoever spreads slander is a fool.
Many words are never free of sin, but whoever holds back his lips is wise.

versions.text: Where words are many, sin is not far behind, but whoever restrains his lips is wise.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew says transgression "does not cease" where words are many; "not far behind" weakens this into mere sequence. The revision keeps the sense that sin is inevitably present and reads with a tighter rhythm.

text: The tongue of the righteous is choice silver; the heart of the wicked is worth little.
The lips of the righteous nourish many, but fools die for lack of sense.
The blessing of the LORD makes rich, and toil adds nothing to it.^f Or: and he adds no sorrow with it.

versions.text: The blessing of the LORD makes rich, and toil adds nothing to it.
versions.explanation: The second line is genuinely ambiguous in Hebrew: עֶצֶב can mean either "toil" or "sorrow," and the subject may be the LORD. A brief footnote noting the alternative rendering would help readers without disturbing the chosen text.

text: Doing wrong is sport to a fool, but wisdom is the delight of a man of understanding.
What the wicked dreads will come upon him, but the desire of the righteous will be granted.
When the storm has passed, the wicked is gone, but the righteous stands on an everlasting foundation.
Like vinegar to the teeth and smoke to the eyes, so is the sluggard to those who send him.
The fear of the LORD adds length to life, but the years of the wicked are cut short.
The hope of the righteous ends in joy, but the expectation of the wicked comes to nothing.
The way of the LORD is a stronghold to the blameless, but ruin to those who do evil.
The righteous will never be shaken, but the wicked will not remain in the land.
The mouth of the righteous brings forth wisdom, but the perverse tongue will be cut off.
The lips of the righteous know what is fitting, but the mouth of the wicked knows only what is perverse.
